question: Should `toolsAllow` become a supported public Gateway and persisted subagent-session capability, including a defined fail-closed contract for CLI-backed child runtimes?
rationale: This is an additive security-sensitive API and session-state contract; source-level cleanup can align wording and tests, but it cannot choose the intended long-term behavior or compatibility promise.

options.title: Adopt a fail-closed cross-runtime contract
options.body: Support the field only where every runtime can enforce it or return a clear error, document that behavior, and retain the session persistence semantics.

options.title: Limit the feature to embedded child runs
options.body: Reject the field for CLI-backed runs and keep the public documentation and tests explicit about that narrower supported surface.

options.title: Pause the public API addition
options.body: Keep the existing configuration-based policy model until maintainers decide the appropriate Gateway and persisted-session abstraction.

recommendation.title: Adopt a fail-closed cross-runtime contract
recommendation.body: Support the field only where every runtime can enforce it or return a clear error, document that behavior, and retain the session persistence semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline explicitly routes the original review toward this person, and the remaining decision is product and security-contract acceptance rather than a mechanical repair.
